record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: Do common turbulence features exist across independently performed 3D3V kinetic simulations using different numerical models, in a way that would demonstrate a genuine universality of kinetic-scale plasma turbulence? This requires separating robust, model-independent properties from differences caused by the large-scale driving, box size, filtering choices, reduced mass ratios, or the distinction between hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic physics.

evidence.quote: we combine data from our recent 3D3V studies ... to investigate whether common turbulence features exist in all three independently performed simulations ... thus indicating a certain "universality" of kinetic-scale turbulence
the process(es) underlying a possible universality of kinetic-range plasma turbulence (e.g., magnetic reconnection) need to be fully worked out

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider three-dimensional, three-velocity (3D3V) kinetic simulations of magnetized collisionless plasma turbulence in a periodic cubic domain, in which the plasma is driven at large scales and the turbulent cascade extends down to and below the ion kinetic scales (the ion gyroradius and ion inertial length). Different simulations may use different numerical models, including (i) fully kinetic Vlasov–Maxwell or particle-in-cell descriptions of both ions and electrons, and (ii) hybrid-kinetic descriptions in which ions are treated kinetically and electrons are treated as a (possibly massless) neutralizing fluid. Simulations may also differ in their large-scale driving mechanism, in box size, in spectral or hyper-dissipative filtering choices, and, in the fully kinetic case, in the (often artificially reduced) ion-to-electron mass ratio.

Define a "universal kinetic-scale turbulence feature" as a statistical property of the turbulent fluctuations at scales near and below the ion kinetic scales—such as the slope and shape of the magnetic, electric, and density power spectra, the spectral anisotropy with respect to the local mean magnetic field, intermittency exponents and structure functions, the distribution and morphology of current sheets and reconnection sites, the partitioning of energy dissipation between ions and electrons, and ion and electron velocity-space structures—whose value, up to controlled corrections, is independent of the choice of numerical model and of the above simulation parameters.

Problem. Determine whether such universal kinetic-scale turbulence features exist. More precisely:

(a) Identify a (possibly empty) set of statistical observables of 3D3V collisionless plasma turbulence whose values at sub-ion scales agree, within quantifiable error bars, across independently performed hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic 3D3V simulations after suitable normalization (e.g., to the ion gyroradius, ion inertial length, and rms turbulent amplitude).

(b) For each such observable, separate the contribution that is robust under variation of the driving prescription, box size, filtering/dissipation, mass ratio, and hybrid-versus-fully-kinetic treatment from contributions that depend on these choices, and provide explicit scalings or bounds for the dependence on each parameter.

(c) Identify the underlying physical mechanism(s) (for example, magnetic reconnection in a sea of intermittent current sheets, kinetic Alfvén wave turbulence, stochastic heating, or Landau/cyclotron damping) responsible for the universal features identified in (a), and derive their statistical predictions from first principles in a way that reproduces the measured universal observables.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of universality of kinetic-scale plasma turbulence across different 3D3V simulation models is a long-standing open problem in plasma physics. Reviews and recent simulation studies (e.g., Cerri, Grošelj, Franci and collaborators) report broadly similar sub-ion spectral slopes and intermittency signatures in hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic runs, but the underlying mechanism(s) and the precise model-independence remain unresolved and are still the subject of active investigation as of 2025–2026.
